"Cursed Birds":
View attachment 4585140 View attachment 4585230
"Bleed":
View attachment 4585237
"Red-ish Light District":
View attachment 4585234 View attachment 4585236
She talks about how she has often deceived Sensei and/or the reader (see first screenshot above this), something that Tsubasa is known for.
"You & Me Against the World":
View attachment 4585275
View attachment 4585274
"The Pleasures of the Flesh":
View attachment 4585288 View attachment 4585289
She speaks directly to Rin, reprimanding her for being too timid and goading her to make a move on Sensei.
View attachment 4585292 View attachment 4585293 View attachment 4585294 View attachment 4585296
It's extremely rare for a narrator to speak to one of the girls directly; in fact, while I'm probably forgetting some, the only other case I can remember is when narrator Tsubasa spoke to Rin during the first beach trip.
View attachment 4585297 View attachment 4585300 View attachment 4585302
The 0.47 narrator wants Rin to drown herself in the wishing well and be decisive about pursuing Sensei. The beach narrator also talked about drowning, the wishing well, and taking what you want.
"See You in the Morning":
View attachment 4585305
View attachment 4585304
"Under My Wing":
View attachment 4587267
At the beach, it seems like Rin might have heard the narrator. If she's hearing the narrator again, that might be the "dark entity" that is influencing her horniness for Sensei.
"See You in the Morning":
View attachment 4585308 View attachment 4585309
"Voice of Reason" & "Dear Sensei (Red Sea)":
View attachment 4585314 View attachment 4585316
One last possible hint, specifically for the reader: Chika mentions that Rin has goosebumps in "Love Long Overdue", which calls back to when narrator Tsubasa discussed Rin and Chika's goosebumps in "The Depressing Implication of Goosebumps" and then again talked about Chika's goosebumps at the onsen.
Preemptive warning: anyone who disagrees with this post lacks the mental capabilities of a 10 year old. And is Bingoogus's alt. And also his boyfriend. And also Selebus's alt trying to gaslight me. Basically I'm saying there's no other possible explanation for these clues.
Click to expand...
Blimey, How could I miss that Rin said the same thing as Tsubasa?! I wonder how many details have I left out in early content (I only developed habit of screenshot every time after a while).
Or perhaps, I was focusing on another thing when they talked about swimming teaching...

Back to Rika being old girlfriend of Tsubasa. I just do think it might be Rie that was her girlfriend.
Yeah Tsubasa did say that she and Wakana studied in Higashigaoka (東が丘? Hill of East. I wonder why Sel came up with a concrete name here) Girls' Academy. I don't think Sekai ever had chance to reach it since Arakawa family doesn't seem to be wealthy enough. And the way she described sneaking away with her girlfriend might indictate her girlfriend was a part of upper class like her (or not, it's too ambiguous and inconclusive to be honest). And as we know, Rie was suggested to have good upbringing.
If Tsubasa needed to sneak away with someone. They had to be together at some level and it's quite possible that they went to the same school and if that's so, Wakana would recognize Rika from the start, which didn't.

spoilers.title: learning to swim
spoilers.html:
When she was in high school, Tsubasa used to sneak away from her strict family to have "wild" experiences with a group of girlfriends. I suggested before that one of those friends was Chiaki, and others have suggested Sekai.
View attachment 4585110 View attachment 4585115
Tsubasa said that one of her girlfriends introduced her to the idea of throwing a child into a pool to force them to swim.
View attachment 4585120 View attachment 4585123
This is also how Rin's mom attempted to teach her to swim.
View attachment 4585124 View attachment 4585126
The "foster mom" part is weird, but elsewhere ("The Art of Never Knowing") she implies that it was her adoptive parents. I guess they fostered her first.
View attachment 4585127
View attachment 4585129
Being forced to swim is widely used as a metaphor in the game, and in fact Tsubasa is using it to describe Touka and Sensei's upcoming relationship, but there was no reason for Selebus to insert the info that the story is literally true for Tsubasa's friend. Rin is the only other person that the story is literally true for. I don't think Selebus would have two characters have identical experiences as sheer coincidence, so I think the two stories are connected.

My speculation is that Rin's mom learned to swim by this method and, since it was effective for her, she both told her friend Tsubasa about it and tried to use it with her own daughter. As for which mom, Rika seems more likely than Rie to have "wild" youthful experiences and engage in irresponsible parenting. On the other hand, given Rie's conservative upbringing it's possible she attended the same prestigious girls' academy as Tsubasa.

Of course, Rika would have no reason to keep an old relationship with Tsubasa secret, so it would be revealed as soon as we saw the two meet - but I'm almost positive that they've yet to appear in a scene together.

I also like the idea that Rika and Chiaki were part of the same friend group but Rika is too thick to connect Chiaki and Chika as two bleach blonde Filipinos whose names starts Chi-. After all, this is the woman who:
  • Came to the conclusion that S.A. Nagahara just happened to look extremely similar to Nodoka and didn't consider the idea that her book was about the class.
  • Didn't consider (until seeing her picture) the possibility that the awkwardly horny girl named Rin who was sexting Sensei was Sensei's awkwardly horny student named Rin.

First time poster here. Just had some
Intro
I think the wishing well is a term Selebus uses to refer to an idea that is a little difficult to nail down, but basically just being the collective unconscious. I understand it just well enough to hint at explaining it, but basically it is a psychological term for the source of dreams and things in our subconscious whose existence we do not owe to ourselves.

Proof
I do not have a lot of proof other than translating the meaning of the phrase with this interpretation and seeing how well it fits with the scene. Ex: The idea that all the gods coming from the wishing well could be interpreted as all the creative beings presented to us as gods are just creations from the wishing well(collective unconscious).
The thing that originally gave me this idea was a clip of an interview with Marie-Louise von Franz(a Jungian psychologist) who reffered to the collective unconscious as a well, but I cannot find the clip now.

Implications
In a relatively healthy person, I think of the collective unconscious as manifesting in dreams/ideas of particular themes/archetypes common to all humanity, but in someone like Sensei, I see it as all the voices and hallucinations he/we hear, real or not.

So sayings like:
Throw yourself into the wishing well = revel in your delusions while ignoring reality
well runs dry = no longer hiding from what you can not understand/deal with(integrating the shadow self or coping with someone dying) OR running out of creative ideas(possibly a double meaning for Selebus running out of ideas)

I am no psychologist btw so feel free to correct/disreguard anything I got wrong.
